subject: Clarifying streaming first-chunk vs. batch throughput commitments — NomadHealth pilot
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@nomadhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Cheng <tom.cheng@nomadhealth.com>, ops@nomadhealth.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot SLA question — streaming first-chunk vs. batch throughput

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the call earlier. We're close to finalizing the NomadHealth pilot scope but one outstanding item is the SLA language around streaming vs non-streaming endpoints. Our security and reliability team is asking for explicit commitments for two things: 

- Time-to-first-chunk (we call it "first-chunk") for streaming endpoints (they want a 95th percentile number), and
- Sustained tokens/sec for non-streaming (batch) endpoints during heavy ingestion windows.

For baseline budgeting we proposed these numbers internally: first-chunk <= 450ms (p95) on 8k contexts; sustained batch >= 20 tokens/sec per concurrent request during peak. We understand Redwood has different performance profiles by model and deployment mode, so before we push the contract through procurement, can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to explicit numerical SLOs for the hosted Pilot, or if we'd need to take a carveout/exemption?

I've attached a short doc describing our use cases and peak windows. If this needs an internal exception path or a Dedicated reservation for predictable throughput, please let us know — we'll escalate to procurement.

Thanks,
Lisa
Head of Integrations, NomadHealth
NomadHealth

Attachment: NomadHealth_SLA_Request_20260809.pdf (application/pdf, 124KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@nomadhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA question — streaming first-chunk vs batch throughput

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachment. Quick summary up-front: we can commit to a measurable p95 first-chunk SLA for streaming under two conditions (model family and deployment mode), and we recommend a Dedicated-reservation for tight sustained tokens/sec targets.

A few details so your procurement/security folks have context: 

- Streaming first-chunk (p95): For our curated Llama-3-derived streaming variants on hosted endpoints we can target p95 <= 350–500ms for requests with up to 8k context when the endpoint is in a standard (non-bursting) capacity tier. The exact number varies by model and quantization profile — we normally publish a verified performance profile for the model pinned by the customer.

- Sustained tokens/sec (batch): Our hosted multi-tenant endpoints are optimized for throughput, but we do not guarantee a per-request sustained tokens/sec number at the hosted tier because of noisy-neighbor and routing variability. For a contract-level sustained throughput commit (e.g., 20 tokens/sec per concurrent batch request at peak) we recommend Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pools and autoscale policies. Dedicated lets us put an explicit throughput SLO in the statement of work.

If you're trying to avoid Dedicated, we can propose a middle ground:
- An initial pilot on hosted with a documented performance profile (p95 ranges per model) plus an operational SLA carveout that accepts higher variance during cloud-wide incidents; and
- A guaranteed fall-through: if observed p95 or throughput falls outside the documented thresholds for three consecutive business days, we (Redwood) will provide priority capacity (burst from reserved pool) and coordinate a mitigation plan.

Operational notes: we do prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts which materially improves both first-chunk and sustained token rates for interactive workflows. If NomadHealth can provide a representative prompt set, our Optimize team will run a short profiling job and produce a recommended endpoint config (batching, cache TTLs, quantization).

I'll loop Karthik for the legal/contract wording suggestions and Aditya for engineering constraints. If you'd like, we can schedule a short session to run a scripted load to demonstrate p95 and sustained throughput with your canonical prompt set.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions PM, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA question — streaming first-chunk vs batch throughput

Hi Lisa — looping in a few specifics we typically put in SOW language so procurement gets what it needs: 

1) Streaming first-chunk SLO (hosted pilot): Redwood will provide a model-specific performance profile with p50/p90/p95 numbers for time-to-first-chunk under the documented pilot workload. For the pilot we will commit to a p95 range (example: 300–500ms) for the nominated model variant. This is measured at our ingress point and excludes client-side rendering time.

2) Non-streaming (batch) throughput: For hosted, Redwood provides probabilistic throughput guidance but not a firm per-request sustained tokens/sec guarantee. For firm commitments we include:
   - Dedicated Reserved: guaranteed tokens/sec per concurrent worker as specified in an attachment table;
   - Hosted with carveout: a best-effort throughput SLO and an escalation/fallback clause that includes temporary allocation of priority capacity.

3) Exceptions & SLA credits: If Redwood fails to meet the agreed p95 for first-chunk for three out of five business days in a measurement window, the parties will escalate to a technical review and Redwood will provide either (a) priority capacity for remediation, (b) a pro-rated service credit, or (c) a combined plan. Specific credit calculations are negotiable and tied to the deal size.

4) Measurement and telemetry: We'll provide token-level latency histograms and per-route dashboards for the pilot so your SREs can validate. We'll also agree on test harnesses and controlled load windows for verification.

If the numbers in Mina's note (first-chunk <= 450ms p95; batch >= 20 tokens/sec) are NomadHealth's must-haves, share a prioritized list — we can draft two SOW options: Hosted pilot (with monitoring + fallback) and Dedicated pilot (firm throughput).

-Karthik
Principal Product Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pilot_scope-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18KB)

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@nomadhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2026 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA question — streaming first-chunk vs batch throughput

Thanks Karthik, Mina — that helps a lot. Quick answers from procurement/security: 

- NomadHealth can accept a hosted pilot if you provide concrete measured p95 ranges per model and an operational fallback clause (the three-out-of-five business days escalation you outlined).
- The 20 tokens/sec sustained per concurrent batch request is their desired target but procurement can accept it as a Dedicated SLO only.

Next steps: please send two formal SOW options we can circulate:
A) Hosted Pilot SOW with model-specific p95 ranges, telemetry dashboards, and a remediation/fallback escalation clause.
B) Dedicated Pilot SOW with explicit sustained tokens/sec guarantees and a reserved capacity table.

Can Redwood get these SOW drafts to us by Friday (2026-08-13)? Also we'd like to schedule a 60-minute profiling session next week — Lisa and Tom will provide the prompt set ahead of time.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Lisa
Head of Integrations, NomadHealth
